AND THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THAT READABLE: an abort is a RESULT only when this tool
ANSWERED everything it meant to answer (exit 7). If a selection it DECIDED ON cannot be
APPLIED, the run exits 10 and PROVES NOTHING — the download stopped at the tool's own
failure, so a configuration that would have been raised later could not appear in the log.
SELECTION POLICY (applied to every configuration the API raises):
1. If a 'NoAction' selection exists, choose it. Always.
2. Otherwise, if exactly one permitted selection is offered, take it AND SAY SO LOUDLY.
3. Otherwise leave the configuration unhandled and let the download abort.
